leftEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
leftEvidence.title: Blood outside the gate; reproach outside the camp

points.label: Action and sequence
points.left: Hebrews recalls bodies burned outside the camp and says Jesus suffered outside the gate to sanctify people through his blood, then calls hearers to go outside bearing reproach.
points.right: Christ’s suffering is presented with an example, no deceit, no retaliation, entrusting, sins borne in his body on the tree, wounds, healing, and return to shepherd and overseer.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.
points.right: This later passage uses Crucifixion language inside its own argument without retelling the complete Gospel event.

payload.posture: Both passages connect Jesus’ suffering with a place or object of reproach while addressing hearers’ response.

rightEvidence.role: The cross in letters and later memory
rightEvidence.title: Suffering, wounds, and sins borne on the tree

payload.tension: Hebrews uses camp, gate, altar, blood, and bearing reproach; 1 Peter uses tree, wounds, non-retaliation, and return to the shepherd.
payload.title: Outside the gate / on the tree
